name: ITC Ltd
about: Established in 1910, ITC is the largest cigarette manufacturer and seller in the country. ITC operates in four business segments at present — FMCG Cigarettes, FMCG Others, Paperboards, Paper and Packaging, and Agri Business. [1]

sections.one_liner: ITC is a diversified Indian consumer conglomerate. Q1FY27 revenue fell 11.1% and margin fell to 27%, so check whether margins are breaking.
business: Segments are FMCG Cigarettes, FMCG Others, Paperboards & Packaging, and Agri Business. The screener blurb calls ITC India's largest cigarette maker. [Numbers]
The annual report lists FMCG (30+ brands, 28 crore households), Paperboards, Agri (40 lakh tonnes sourced), Hotels (14,200 keys) and IT (35+ countries). [AR FY26]
Revenue share by segment is not disclosed, so we cannot tell how much profit depends on cigarettes. [AR FY26]
AR gross revenue is ₹80,867cr versus ₹78,868cr reported. The ₹1,999cr gap is not reconciled. [AR FY26] [Numbers]
financial_snapshot: Q1FY27 (Jun-26): revenue ₹19,114cr, down 11.1% YoY. EBITDA ₹5,181cr, down 24% from ₹6,816cr. PAT ₹4,509cr, down 15.6%. [Numbers]
Q1 operating margin was 27%, the lowest in 8 quarters and 12 points below Mar-26's 39%. TTM margin is 33.6% versus 35% for FY26. [Numbers]
TTM revenue ₹76,488cr, EBITDA ₹25,683cr, PAT ₹20,184cr. All three are below FY26 levels, so earnings are now shrinking. [Numbers]
P/E 17x, P/B 4.6x, dividend yield 5.37%. Price ₹267 is 37% below the ₹426 high. ROCE 38.9%, ROE 29.3%. [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue CAGR slowed from 9.9% (5y) to 3.6% (3y). The last two quarters were down 5.0% and 11.1% YoY. [Numbers]
EBITDA grew only 2.0% a year, from ₹25,704cr (FY23) to ₹27,306cr (FY26). Operating margin stayed in a 34–37% band. [Numbers]
FY25 PAT of ₹35,052cr was inflated by a ₹19,808cr Mar-25 quarter; its nature is not disclosed. Underlying PAT is flat: ₹20,751cr FY24, ₹21,018cr FY26. [Numbers]
ROCE rose from 28% (FY21) to 39% (FY26). Returns are high but not growing alongside sales. [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Borrowings rose 8.4x, from ₹285cr to ₹2,399cr in FY26. Debt/equity is 0.03, which is negligible, but the reason for the jump is not disclosed. [Numbers]
The cash conversion cycle stretched from 105 days (FY23) to 164 days (FY26), driven by inventory days rising from 148 to 209. [Numbers]
Net worth fell from ₹74,507cr to ₹70,030cr in FY25 despite ₹35,052cr PAT. Large distributions are implied but not disclosed. [Numbers]
cash_quality: Reported CFO/PAT is 0.69 over 3 years, dragged down by the FY25 one-off. Excluding it, the ratio is about 0.86. FY26 alone is 0.88 (₹18,464cr / ₹21,018cr). [Numbers]
FCF is flat: ₹16,184cr (FY23) and ₹16,332cr (FY26). Implied capex is only about ₹2,100cr a year despite two plants under construction. [Numbers] [AR FY26]
Implied dividend outflow (5.37% × ₹3,34,289cr ≈ ₹17,950cr) exceeds FY26 FCF of ₹16,332cr. Payout is above 100% of FCF. [Numbers]
narrative_vs_numbers: The AR says 'unlock growth'. The numbers show a 3.6% 3y revenue CAGR and Q1FY27 revenue down 11.1% YoY. They disagree. [AR FY26] [Numbers]
The AR claims 'cost agility'. Q1FY27 margin fell 5 points YoY to 27%, and EBITDA fell 24%. Costs did not flex. [AR FY26] [Numbers]
The AR cites 'supply chain structural interventions'. Inventory days instead rose from 178 to 209 in FY26. [AR FY26] [Numbers]
The AR flags commodity and FX volatility as a key risk. The Q1FY27 margin collapse is consistent with that risk materialising, though the cause is not disclosed. [AR FY26] [Numbers]
guidance: No call transcripts were provided. Explicit growth or margin guidance is not disclosed. [Q1FY27 call]
Capex: two integrated consumer goods plants are under construction at Bhiwadi and Sandila. Amount and timing are not disclosed. [AR FY26]
Strategy: value-accretive M&A and new growth areas. No size, budget or target is disclosed. [AR FY26]
Outlook is qualitative only ('challenging global environment'), with no numeric targets. [AR FY26]

ledger.promised: AR FY26: 'cost agility' through supply-chain interventions (no transcript guidance available)
ledger.delivered: Operating margin 27% vs 32% a year ago. EBITDA ₹5,181cr, down 24% YoY.

ledger.promised: AR FY26: leverage synergies and innovation to 'unlock growth'
ledger.delivered: Revenue ₹19,114cr, down 11.1% YoY. The previous quarter was also down, by 5.0%.

ledger.promised: AR FY26: supply chain structural interventions
ledger.delivered: Inventory days 209 vs 178 in FY25. Cash conversion cycle 164 vs 146 days.

ledger.promised: AR FY26: Bhiwadi and Sandila plants under construction
ledger.delivered: FY26 implied capex about ₹2,132cr. No completion date disclosed.

ledger.promised: AR FY26: value-accretive M&A and new growth areas
ledger.delivered: Borrowings up to ₹2,399cr from ₹285cr. No deal or return metric disclosed.

bull: ROCE is 39% and debt/equity 0.03. FCF of ₹16,332cr is steady over 4 years. [Numbers]
P/E 17x with a 5.37% dividend yield, and the price is near its ₹253 low. That looks like a lot of bad news priced in. [Numbers]
Margins held at 34–37% for 6 years. Q1FY27's 27% could be a one-quarter commodity shock if it reverts. [Numbers] [AR FY26]
bear: TTM EBITDA and PAT are both below FY26 levels. Underlying PAT has been flat at about ₹21,000cr since FY24. [Numbers]
Dividends of about ₹17,950cr exceed FCF of ₹16,332cr, and borrowings rose 8.4x. The yield may not be fully covered by cash. [Numbers]
Inventory days went from 148 to 209 in 3 years, tying up working capital. That caps cash conversion at about 0.86–0.88. [Numbers]
questions: What drove the Q1FY27 margin drop to 27%: commodities, mix, or one-offs?
What was the ₹19,808cr Mar-25 PAT item, and will it recur?
Why did borrowings rise to ₹2,399cr, and what is the money funding?
How much will Bhiwadi and Sandila cost, and when will they add revenue?

annual_report.revenue_mix: Diversified across consumer goods, paperboards, hotels, IT services. Domestic reach 28 crore households plus international presence in 35+ countries.
strategy: Strengthen core brands via value-added adjacencies and new categories
Mainline AI, digital-first culture across operations
Supply chain structural interventions and cost agility
Value-accretive M&A and emerging growth vectors
